about: The signer's rule of Verifiable Intent (lcp profile card-mastercard-vi.md, rule 7): VI's reference verifier checks each signature over its own re-encoding of the JSON it parses, json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":")) (agent-intent/verifiable-intent at 356c296, src/verifiable_intent/crypto/sd_jwt.py), so a signer signs JSON that re-encoding leaves unchanged. Each row's expect is what CPython 3.12.3's json module writes for the value it reads from the row's json: json.dumps(json.loads(json), separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True), run with python3 -I on 2026-11-17, outside this repository. Both languages read each row's json with their own JSON parser and write it by the rule, giving expect. No number is written integral with a fraction or an exponent, which JSON.parse reads as an integer and Python as a float, and none is an integer past 2^53 - 1, which JSON.parse rounds. The last three rows are segments of the Verifiable Intent strings of @integraledger/lcp's vectors/card.json (vi.CJ, vi.L2i), which the rule leaves unchanged.

fractions Python and JavaScript write alike
fractions below 1e-4, which Python writes with a two-digit exponent
